title: Designing Domain-Specific Large Language Models - The Critical Role of Fine-Tuning in Public Opinion Simulation

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM-generated public opinion distributions for synthetic profiles (varying by age, gender, and ethnicity) against real-world survey data from the UK Household Longitudinal Study (UKHLS) dataset using statistical metrics such as Chi-Square tests, Cosine Similarity, Jaccard Index, and KL-divergence, as well as applying fairness metrics like Demographic Parity Difference (DPD) and Equal Opportunity Difference (EOD).

Evaluating the alignment of simulated policy opinions (e.g., support for carbon taxes) against expected real-world data across different income brackets, professions, and educational backgrounds to ensure the model captures nuanced economic divides.

Measuring the differences in generated environmental opinions between profiles assigned to urban versus rural living areas and specific UK regions to check for and mitigate oversimplified, uniform consensus responses.

Using counterfactual profile substitution with varying voting intentions (e.g., Green Party vs. Reform UK) to assess the model's capacity to accurately simulate polarized, ideologically driven attitudes toward climate change policies.
